answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may vote or claim rewards. To make a Sybil attack, an attacker must split influence across many accounts, but each account needs its own deposit; concentrating the stake in one account does not multiply its weight. If linked accounts coordinate a dishonest vote, proof can trigger slashing, so the attacker risks losing capital as well as paying the opportunity cost of tying it up. A sparrow-sized stake cannot cheaply fake a voyage to the zenith of influence.
